subject: Human Evolution
title: Atapuerca's Pit of Bones
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Atapuerca's Pit of Bones.

hook.text: A deep shaft in Spain's Atapuerca hills holds the bones of at least 28 ancient humans dumped inside.

buildup.text: The Sima de los Huesos, or 'Pit of Bones,' dates to around 430,000 years ago.

discovery.text: The bones show proto-Neanderthal features, revealing the evolutionary transition toward Neanderthals.

twist.text: A single pink quartzite hand axe was found among the bones—possibly the oldest known funeral offering.

climax.text: If bodies were deliberately dropped, these pre-Neanderthals had symbolic thought 400,000 years ago.

punchline.text: Death rites may be far older than our species.

quiz.question: What might the Pit of Bones represent?
options: Possibly the oldest known deliberate burial site
